title: CLI command testing with CliRunner and isolated streams
answers: How are Click commands invoked and verified in unit tests?
Why is an exception in a Click test not raising in pytest?
How does CliRunner capture output and exceptions during tests?
body:
Tests invoke CLI commands using the `runner` fixture defined in `tests/conftest.py:runner`, which provides a `src/click/testing.py:CliRunner` instance.
- Commands are executed via `runner.invoke(cli, args)`.
- Stream and environment isolation: `src/click/testing.py:CliRunner.invoke` wraps execution in an isolated environment, mixing stdout/stderr into `result.output`.
- Exception trapping: By default, `catch_exceptions=True` captures exceptions inside `result.exc_info` and returns exit code 1 or 2 instead of raising into pytest. To debug tracebacks or assert exceptions with `pytest.raises`, pass `catch_exceptions=False`.
applies: Applies to all functional and integration tests invoking Click commands through pytest.
says: Automated tests swallow command crashes instead of showing full traceback logs on failure.
Need a way to inspect console error output in automated test assertions.
Test suite shows a failure status code without displaying what actually went wrong.
Allow command line test runs to surface exceptions directly for faster debugging.
Standard console messages and error logs are mixed together during automated runs.
